Private, CIN U29113KA2004PTC184018 — a subsidiary of French group Recaero SAS (Verniolle, France, founded 1993), which also owns Recaero Composites, Recaero India and Recaero Formation.

masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: Recaero India: an Airbus-approved supplier whose biggest customer is its own French parent.

subhead.text: A Bidadi, Bangalore precision-machining unit with AS9100D and Airbus Approved Supplier status, mostly feeding Recaero SAS and Safran rather than the open market.

p1_engine.eyebrow: A genuinely certified capability, mostly serving its own group

blocks.text: Revenue reached ₹151 Cr in FY25, up 8.96% year-on-year — steady, if not fast, growth — with no PAT, EBITDA margin or ROE figure found for the standalone India entity.

Its AS9100D and Airbus Approved Supplier certifications are third-party sourced to an actual TUV SUD certificate document, not just a company claim — the strongest-credibility moat evidence available for this company, even though the HVT sheet still marks it `needs_verify: yes`.
blocks.source: HVT row (third-party, TUV SUD certificate); recaero.fr

blocks.text: **A structural nuance worth naming plainly**: the HVT sheet's own gap research, sourced to trade data, states that Recaero India's major buyers are Recaero France (its own parent) and Safran Aircraft Engine — meaning a meaningful share of its 'export' activity is intra-group, not open-market sales to external customers. This isn't a red flag (captive manufacturing arms are a normal model in aerospace), but it changes what 'export capability' means here.

It runs 17+ CNC machines (up to 9-axis, 3-axis turn-mill) machining aluminum, Inconel, titanium and 15-5PH alloys, plus a dedicated sheet-metal shop and OEM-qualified welding (TIG, Plasma, Spot) — real, specific manufacturing capability across the hardest aerospace alloys.

insights.point: The field is **large and structurally favored by India's own policy direction.**
insights.evidence: India aerospace parts manufacturing: $13.6B (2023) to $21.48B by 2030 (6.8%/yr); India's defense indigenization is expected to rise from under 40% to potentially 70%+ over the coming decade.

insights.point: **AS9100/NADCAP certification is the real gate**, and Recaero India already clears it — the harder question is whether that clearance is being used beyond the group.
insights.evidence: AS9100 certification functions as a de facto requirement for OEM approved-vendor-list status; Recaero India holds it independently of its parent relationship, meaning the qualification itself could support external customers too.

insights.point: The closest listed peer shows **what a genuinely externally-diversified version of this business looks like.**
insights.evidence: Azad Engineering posts ₹590 Cr revenue (+30% YoY) with 36.9% EBITDA margin, supplying GE, Honeywell, Rolls-Royce, Safran and Siemens as named external customers, plus new contracts with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Baker Hughes — a materially more diversified customer base than Recaero India's current parent-plus-Safran concentration.

reflect.text: A genuinely certified, well-equipped precision-machining operation whose customer base is still mostly its own French parent group. The certification is real and portable — the question is whether the company will use it to diversify beyond the family.

p2_market.sourceNote: Market data: Grand View Research, soic.in (shared aerospace-precision-machined-components segment file). Peer data: Azad Engineering (a materially more externally-diversified comparable).

p3_opportunities.lede: One clear place worth watching, named directly in the company's own gap research.

items.title: Expanding export activity to external global buyers beyond Recaero SA
items.body: The HVT sheet's own gap research names this directly: current export activity is concentrated on the parent group (Recaero France) and Safran, with clear stated potential to expand to external global buyers beyond the family group — the AS9100D/Airbus-approved certification already exists to support that expansion.
items.source: HVT gap research (Volza trade data on Recaero SA).

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions. Which would work, and how much, only Recaero India's own data and people can tell. Each is small, made to learn fast.

items.title: Pursue one external OEM RFQ using existing AS9100D/Airbus credentials
items.body: Use the already-earned AS9100D and Airbus Approved Supplier status to respond to one external OEM's RFQ (outside the Recaero/Safran relationship) as a test case, measuring how much of the qualification burden the existing certifications actually remove.

takeaway.text: A genuinely certified, well-equipped aerospace machining shop, still mostly serving its own family. **The Airbus approval is real — using it beyond the parent group is the open question.**
